days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday's soggy morning gives way to a gorgeous fall weekend. The rain tapers off this afternoon with a high in the mid 60s, and the evening dries out around 60. Saturday is sunny and crisp with a high near 59 and a light north wind, but it cools off fast after dark, down to around 41 overnight. Sunday is mostly sunny and a few degrees warmer with a high near 65 and a breezy south wind, and clouds move in Sunday night ahead of a cold front with a chance of showers Monday morning. Frost looks likely Tuesday and Wednesday mornings behind it, and the leaves in most of the high terrain are peaking right on time. Track it all week, with patio, swim, and sunset scores, at Burlington Right Now .

days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday kicks off UVM Weekend , three days of games, open houses and reunions all over campus that are free to register for. At 12:30 Murmurations Aerial on Flynn Avenue runs Silver Wings , an intro aerial fabric workshop designed for folks 50 and up. At 2 Shelburne Museum director Thomas Denenberg talks about Norman Rockwell in Vermont at the EEE lecture series at Faith United Methodist Church in South Burlington, and VTIFF screens The Work in Progress , the follow up to Robert Reich's The Last Class, where 30 and 80 year olds ask each other about democracy and community, at 4 and again at 7 at the Film House.

days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday night fills up fast. Hula hosts a free movie night at 6 with The Water We Belong To, about the Burlington Surf Club community, and the premiere of Wave Man, and at 7 Dad Guild's Book It! Pizza Party gets dads together at the Soda Plant to talk about whatever book they read, with a personal pan pizza for everyone. Also at 7, the Shelburne Players open Hatchford Hotel , a brand new musical set in a suspiciously familiar corner of Vermont, Merit Kahn brings her one woman comedy show Optimistic Personality Disorder to Off Center (also Saturday at 7 and Sunday at 5), and the Double E in Essex starts three nights of Phish webcast parties from Atlantic City. At 7:30 the UVM Lane Series brings the Tesla Quartet to the Recital Hall with Haydn, Bacewicz and Schumann (students $7.73), and Alex Toth of Rubblebucket plays Higher Ground as Tōth with doors at 7:30. Winooski songwriter Erin Cassels-Brown plays Monkey House at 8 behind his debut album, Dreamin' On Overdrive.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday starts with us. BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] is at Zero Gravity at 10, so come find us. Earlier birds can run or walk the RALLYTHON 5K on UVM's Gutterson loop at 9, a $20 benefit for the Golisano Children's Hospital, and the Burlington Farmers Market runs 9 to 2 on Pine Street. Also from 9, the 32nd annual SBHS Ski & Board Sale fills Tuttle Middle School in South Burlington with new and used gear, the Williston Woods Annual Bazaar has crafts, a bake sale and homemade soups for lunch, and city arborist Nick Garty leads a free tree walk through City Center Park in South Burlington. At 10 the artists at Shelburne Pond Studios open their barn studios until 4, and the Rozalia Project hosts a waterfront cleanup in downtown Winooski. At 10:30 Rock Point leads a free phenology walk on its trails, and the Forever 38 group goes apple picking [MEETUP] at Shelburne Orchards, where Will Behm and Eliza Goodell play old time fiddle and guitar at noon for Live in the Orchard .

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday morning, the Long Trail Running Club runs the whole Wildways Trail [MEETUP] from Leddy Park at 9, about 12.4 miles with a 4 mile option, at a conversational, no drop pace. At 10 the Harborvale eases into Sunday with live classical music until noon, the Burlington Vintage Market takes over Foam for its fifth anniversary with 30+ dealers and DJs until 7, and the Walk to End Alzheimer's opens registration at Shelburne Museum ahead of the 2 mile walk at 11:30. Also at 10, the Burlington Letter Writing Group meets at Zero Gravity, Steps to End Domestic Violence marks its 50th year with the Take Steps for Survivors 5K and 10K at Oakledge, and the Winooski Farmers Market has Bikes, Berries & Bumpouts with bike powered smoothies and tune ups by donation. All day Sunday, the Odd Fellows host 24 Hour Comics Day , a 12 hour draw-a-thon with local cartoonists on hand and pizza and snacks included ($15 suggested, no one turned away).
